findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. A newcomer can say what this is and why it matters after one paragraph.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The heading names firstmate, which a newcomer has never heard of, before it says what Athena is. Someone who arrived at Athena's home page may think they are on the wrong site until the second paragraph explains that this page is a sample study.

A next-step link sits in the header and goes to a concrete Next steps section with prerequisites, a clone command, `./setup.sh` and a sample `athena ask "add a changelog"` run. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The header promises traceable models, costs and verdicts, but the page never shows any of these for its own study. The study is a reading of another project, so it does not show a commit, a cost or a verdict that would back up the main selling point.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: This header link is meant for the project owner, yet it addresses a newcomer as 'your decision'. A first-time reader has no proposals and may not understand what this link is for.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: Key words get defined before they are used, and there is a full glossary, which helps. But the same definitions also repeat in the transition cards and the claims, so the page is long and dense for a reader who only wants the gist.
findings.source: Words used first ... Each is defined here, and again in the Glossary at the end of the page.

findings.text: Most of the page covers firstmate's internal details: exit codes, locks, pending-close records. That depth is a good demonstration of rigour, but a newcomer will probably skim it. Nothing tells them they can skip from Start here straight to Next steps.
findings.source: Transitions: t1 to t12 cards, e.g. "places-held at or above the declared capacity (checked by code)" and "exits 75"

findings.text: The Limits section uses Athena's internal jargon ('the job', 'recorded boundary') without explaining it, so a newcomer cannot follow it.
findings.source: f1 ... The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate, so no failure or retry edge was observed

findings.text: The About section points to a `studies/` folder but gives no link and does not say which repository it is in. A newcomer is left guessing.
findings.source: This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from.
